sources.title: Obsidian Rocks — How I use folders in Obsidian
sources.claim: Tim Miller uses only 5 workflow folders (FINVA); argues folders force exclusivity that hurts as projects grow.

sources.title: Steph Ango — My vault
sources.claim: Steph Ango (Obsidian CEO) uses ~4 folders and organises via links/properties; navigates with Quick Switcher and backlinks, not the file tree.

sources.title: Shuvangkar Das — Obsidian note organization
sources.claim: Recommends shallow folders + MOCs + tags as discovery signals; tags are signals not structure; cap nesting at ~2 levels.

sources.title: Obsidian Help — Backlinks
sources.claim: Official Obsidian docs define backlinks pane with Linked Mentions and Unlinked Mentions sections.

sources.title: Medium — Obsidian: between MOCs and tags
sources.claim: MOCs and tags are complementary not opposing; MOCs are curated frozen state, tags qualify status.

sources.title: Obsidian Forum — MOC vs tagging
sources.claim: Forum users argue MOCs allow description/ordering/formatting that tags can't; recommend starting with tags and adding MOCs only when needed.

sources.title: dsebastien — Maps of Content
sources.claim: MOCs are 'folders on steroids' — a note can appear in multiple MOCs unlike folders; types include basic, contextual, and meta-MOCs.

sources.title: Obsidian Forum — The ultimate folder system (ACE)
sources.claim: Nick Milo's ACE = Atlas, Calendar, Efforts; based on STIR model; Relatedness is handled via links not folders.

sources.title: Linking Your Thinking (LYT)
sources.claim: LYT framework popularised MOCs; community testimony of going folderless then re-adding a few folders for balance.

sources.title: MakeUseOf — Orphan notes in Obsidian
sources.claim: System for linking 500 orphan notes: one wikilink per new note, Graph View to spot orphans, 3 MOCs to absorb them, #needs-link weekly batch.

sources.title: Obsidian Help — Link notes
sources.claim: Official Obsidian: linking notes is the platform's core power; non-existent links appear muted, acting as future seeds.

sources.title: Aidan Helfant — 5 levels of MOC mastery
sources.claim: Five-level MOC adoption progression: isolated notes → linking → first MOC (Dump/Lump/Jump) → MOC-of-MOCs → Home note. 'Think and link first.'

sources.title: Learning Aloud — Unlinked mentions
sources.claim: Strategic title selection makes unlinked mentions surface free connections; works as low-maintenance retrieval layer.

sources.title: AI Maker — PARA Method with Obsidian
sources.claim: PARA (Projects, Areas, Resources, Archives) — Tiago Forte's cross-tool method, frequently used as an Obsidian scaffold.

sources.title: Brandon K. Boswell — Should you use PARA in Obsidian?
sources.claim: Recommends against strict PARA in Obsidian; argues folder exclusivity fights graph structure; selective borrowing only.

sources.title: XDA — Obsidian folder setup that finally clicks
sources.claim: Cautions against 'creating for the graph' — writing pointless notes or forcing links just to see new dots.

sources.title: Digest Africa — Mastering backlinks in Obsidian
sources.claim: Avoid circular backlinks (A→B, B→A with no semantic value) as a backlink antipattern.
